newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil welcomes new U.S. rules on gasoline imports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil welcomes new U.S. rules on gasoline imports.

text.p: The Brazilian government Monday welcomed a decision by the United States to make imported gasoline subject to the same environmental regulations as U.S. gasoline, ending a long-running trade dispute.

The move will help Brazil's state-owned petroleum company Petrobras resume it exports of gasoline to the United States, Regis Aslanian, head of the Brazilian Foreign Ministry's foreign trade department, told reporters.
"The fact that the Americans are observing a ruling of the World Trade Organization is of great importance to Brazil," Aslanian said.

Petrobras' gasoline exports to the United States, which totalled $285 million in 1993, were halted in January 1995 when the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) introduced different requirements for imported and U.S. gasoline.
Aslanian said U.S. refineries were allowed to continue using existing quality baselines while foreign refineries were required to match the average baselines of U.S. refineries in 1990.

Brazil and Venezuela, both of which were affected by the rules, challenged the regulations in a panel at the World Trade Organization which in May 1995 ruled in their favor, requesting the United States review its legislation.

The new rules, which were due to be published May 6 in the Federal Register, the offical gazette of the U.S. government, would also benefit PDVSA, Venezuela's oil giant whose exports were also affected by the old rules, Aslanian said.
